title: record-alert `severity: 'success'` renders a Database glyph, not a check mark — `CheckCircle2` is dead on BOTH lucide surfaces
body:
Found by the #5936 slice's dev while censusing icon literals, handed to the PM rather than fixed (out of that card's two-site fence, and the icon gate does not judge this site — a repair there needs a new pin, which the bounded in-place exemption forbids). Re-measured in full by the `domain:ui` PM seat before filing. Filed unassigned.

## The defect

`packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/record-alert.tsx`:

```ts
success: {
  wrap: 'border-emerald-300/60 bg-emerald-50 …',
  icon: 'CheckCircle2',
},
```

That string reaches `<LazyIcon name={iconName} … />` in the same file. `CheckCircle2` resolves to nothing, and `getLazyIcon` **silently degrades to the `Database` glyph**.

⇒ **Every `record-alert` with `severity: 'success'` paints a database icon where a check mark belongs.** Green wrap, emerald text, database glyph.

## Why it is silent

`packages/components/src/lib/lazy-icon.tsx`:

```ts
import { Database } from 'lucide-react';
import { DynamicIcon, iconNames } from 'lucide-react/dynamic.mjs';
const VALID_ICON_NAMES: Set<string> = new Set(iconNames as string[]);
…
const kebab = toKebabIconName(name);
if (!isLucideIcon(kebab)) {
  cache.set(name, Database);
  return Database;               // :71-73
}
```

The fallback is deliberate and correct in general — its own comment says server-driven schemas often reference icons from other libraries, so it degrades rather than throwing. It is the *right* default for an authored schema slot and the *wrong* outcome for a hardcoded platform constant, which is what this is.

## Measured

`lucide-react@1.31.0` — the version `packages/plugin-detail` resolves.

**The dynamic surface** — the one that decides, because this file goes through `LazyIcon`:

```
iconNames size: 2025
CheckCircle2  -> check-circle2  in iconNames : false     <-- the defect
CircleCheck   -> circle-check   in iconNames : true
LIT  control  circle-check                   : true
DARK control  no-such-glyph-xyz              : false
```

**The record surface**, for completeness:

```
CheckCircle2 in icons record : false
CircleCheck  in icons record : true
LIT  control icons.Info      : true
DARK control icons.Xyzzy     : false
```

Dead on **both**. Every zero above sits beside a control in the same query shape that fires.

## The correct spelling, derived by identity rather than remembered

```
CheckCircle2 === icons.CircleCheck : true
```

Same glyph object. ⇒ the live spelling is **`circle-check`**, present on both surfaces, and the repair is a substitution-free rename — it cannot change which glyph is drawn, only whether one is drawn at all.

## ⭐ The three neighbours are NOT defects — do not "fix" them

`SEVERITY_STYLES`'s other icons are `Info`, `AlertTriangle` and `AlertCircle`, and **all three are also absent from the `icons` record**. A census that stopped at the record would report four defects and be wrong about three:

| name | record | dynamic (`iconNames`) | renders? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Info` | absent | **present** | ✅ correctly |
| `AlertTriangle` | absent | **present** | ✅ correctly |
| `AlertCircle` | absent | **present** | ✅ correctly |
| `CheckCircle2` | absent | **absent** | ❌ Database glyph |

Which surface a site resolves through decides whether a retired spelling is a defect or a non-event, and this file resolves through the dynamic one. #5622 documented that two-surface split (record 1767 entries vs dynamic 2025, disagreeing about aliases); its own cases were record-surface misses that the dynamic surface still carried. **This one is the other kind** — dead on both — which is why #5622's sweep did not catch it.

## Reproduce

```
sed -n '158,170p' packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/record-alert.tsx   # the declaration
node -e "const {iconNames}=require('lucide-react/dynamic.mjs');const S=new Set(iconNames);
  console.log('check-circle2:',S.has('check-circle2'));   // false — the defect
  console.log('circle-check :',S.has('circle-check'));    // true  — LIT control
  console.log('alert-triangle:',S.has('alert-triangle')); // true  — the neighbour is fine
  console.log('no-such-xyz  :',S.has('no-such-xyz'));"    // false — DARK control
```

## Suggested scope

1. One-line rename `'CheckCircle2'` → `'circle-check'`.
2. ⭐ **A pin, which is the load-bearing half.** The icon gate (`check-lucide-icon-record-names.mjs`) explicitly does **not** judge dynamic-surface resolvers — it says so in its own verdict line (*"dynamic surface 4 sites, 2025 names, not judged here"*). So this site is invisible to the gate in both directions: nothing caught the defect, and nothing would catch its regression. The honest repair pins every `SEVERITY_STYLES` icon as resolvable on the surface it actually resolves through.
3. ⚠️ Consider whether the other `SEVERITY_STYLES` names should move to their live spellings too. They render correctly today, so this is hygiene, not a fix — and #5622 already noted that a dead-for-lookup spelling sitting in a map is how the last one got copied around.

## Not in scope

⛔ Changing `getLazyIcon`'s `Database` fallback. It is deliberate and documented, and `isLucideIconName` is already exported precisely so a caller with a better fallback can ask first. Whether `record-alert` should ask first is a separate question from whether its constant is spelled correctly.

## Dedup

`search_issues` for `CheckCircle2` / `record-alert severity success glyph` returns only #5936 (matched by this finding's own comment on it). ⭐ Run **with a live positive control** in the same pass — an earlier attempt tonight returned `total_count: 0` while the control call was refused by a rate limit, which makes the zero uninterpretable; that reading was discarded and not filed on. Related, all closed and none covering this site: #5622 (record-surface misses, `edit`/`smile`), #5586 (the plugin-view half), #5633 / PR #5932 (the gate). Full working: [#5936 comment 5535124203](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/issues/5936#issuecomment-5535124203).

## ⚠️ Unmeasured

Whether any shipped metadata actually authors `severity: 'success'` on a `record-alert`. The defect is proven from source; its field frequency is not.
